title: Finding the Writing Pocket
use_cases: Use when coaching writers on architectural description techniques
Implement when editing manuscripts to improve prose rhythm
Configure when establishing a balance between detail and narrative pacing
Use when seeking metaphors to explain the intuitive nature of storytelling
content:
Good writing, like good music, has a natural flow and rhythm. When coaching writers on description, I often draw parallels to music because both require:

1. Author Page
2. A sense of when to add detail and when to pull back
3. The discipline to serve the overall story
4. The ability to create momentum and forward movement
5. An intuitive feel for what “sounds right” to the reader

When editing a manuscript with clunky description, I often tell the writer: “This isn’t a math problem. It’s like riding a bike. You lean one way, you lean the other way, you keep falling over. Eventually, with practice and feedback, you find your balance.”
